name_translation: The Yoga of Knowledge, Action, and Renunciation

verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
इमं विवस्वते योगं प्रोक्तवानहमव्ययम् |
विवस्वान्मनवे प्राह मनुरिक्ष्वाकवेऽब्रवीत् || १ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
imaṃ vivasvate yogaṃ proktavānahamavyayam |
vivasvānmanave prāha manurikṣvākave'bravīt || 1 ||
verses.translation: The Supreme Lord said: I taught this imperishable science of Yoga to the Sun-god Vivasvan; Vivasvan passed it on to Manu, the father of mankind; and Manu imparted it unto King Ikshvaku.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna establishes the primordial, timeless antiquity of Yoga. By showing that this wisdom was originally entrusted to the solar deity and passed down to royal sages (Rajarshis), Krishna emphasizes that spiritual discipline and selfless governance are meant to guide the leaders of humanity.

verses.text_sanskrit:
एवं परम्पराप्राप्तमिमं राजर्षयो विदुः |
स कालेनेह महता योगो नष्टः परन्तप || २ ||
verses.transliteration:
evaṃ paramparāprāptamimaṃ rājarṣayo viduḥ |
sa kāleneha mahatā yogo naṣṭaḥ parantapa || 2 ||
verses.translation: This supreme science was thus received through an unbroken chain of disciplic succession (Parampara), and the royal sages understood it. But with the great passage of time, O scorcher of foes (Arjuna), that Yoga became lost to the world.
verses.meaning: Wisdom is preserved through authentic teacher-disciple lineages (Guru-Shishya Parampara). When disciples lose self-discipline and compromise the pure intention of the teachings, the living essence of Yoga decays and disappears from human society.

verses.text_sanskrit:
स एवायं मया तेऽद्य योगः प्रोक्तः पुरातनः |
भक्तोऽसि मे सखा चेति रहस्यं ह्येतदुत्तमम् || ३ ||
verses.transliteration:
sa evāyaṃ mayā te'dya yogaḥ proktaḥ purātanaḥ |
bhakto'si me sakhā ceti rahasyaṃ hyetaduttamam || 3 ||
verses.translation: That very same ancient Yoga is today revealed by Me unto you, because you are My devotee and My dear friend. This is indeed the supreme, confidential mystery.
verses.meaning: Spiritual truth is not unlocked by intellectual arrogance, but through devotion (Bhakti) and loving friendship (Sakhya). Arjuna's pure, receptive heart qualifies him to receive the supreme mystery (Uttamam Rahasyam) of cosmic wisdom directly from the Lord.

verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
अपरं भवतो जन्म परं जन्म विवस्वतः |
कथमेतद्विजानीयां त्वमादौ प्रोक्तवानिति || ४ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
aparaṃ bhavato janma paraṃ janma vivasvataḥ |
kathametadvijānīyāṃ tvamādau proktavāniti || 4 ||
verses.translation: Arjuna said: Your birth took place in recent times, whereas the birth of Vivasvan (the Sun-god) occurred in ancient antiquity. How then am I to understand that You instructed him in the beginning?
verses.meaning: Arjuna voices a natural human paradox: Seeing Sri Krishna in His physical, contemporary form, Arjuna inquires about the mystery of divine descent. This question prompts Krishna to reveal the sublime mystery of His Avatara and eternal transcendence.

verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
बहूनि मे व्यतीतानि जन्मानि तव चार्जुन |
तान्यहं वेद सर्वाणि न त्वं वेत्थ परन्तप || ५ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
bahūni me vyatītāni janmāni tava cārjuna |
tānyahaṃ veda sarvāṇi na tvaṃ vettha parantapa || 5 ||
verses.translation: The Supreme Lord said: Many births have passed for Me and for you, O Arjuna. I know all of them fully, but you remember them not, O scorcher of foes!
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna reveals the fundamental distinction between the Supreme Divine (Ishvara) and the individual soul (Jiva). The individual soul forgets past incarnations due to the veil of Maya, whereas the omniscient Lord possesses unbroken, eternal awareness of all manifestations.

verses.text_sanskrit:
अजोऽपि सन्नव्ययात्मा भूतानामीश्वरोऽपि सन् |
प्रकृतिं स्वामधिष्ठाय संभवाम्यात्ममायया || ६ ||
verses.transliteration:
ajo'pi sannavyayātmā bhūtānāmīśvaro'pi san |
prakṛtiṃ svāmadhiṣṭhāya saṃbhavāmyātmamāyayā || 6 ||
verses.translation: Although I am unborn, imperishable in My nature, and the Lord of all living beings, yet controlling My material energy (Prakriti), I manifest Myself through My own divine power (Atma-Maya).
verses.meaning: Unlike mortal beings who are forced into embodiment by their past karmas, the Supreme Lord descends through sovereign divine will. He remains the unconditioned Master of nature even while assuming a wondrous, visible form in the physical realm.

verses.text_sanskrit:
यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत |
अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदात्मानं सृजाम्यहम् || ७ ||
verses.transliteration:
yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānirbhavati bhārata |
abhyutthānamadharmasya tadātmānaṃ sṛjāmyaham || 7 ||
verses.translation: Whenever and wherever there is a decline in righteousness (Dharma), O descendant of Bharata, and a rampant rise of unrighteousness (Adharma), at that time I manifest Myself upon earth.
verses.meaning: One of the most celebrated shlokas in sacred literature. It guarantees divine intervention in human history. When moral order breaks down and cosmic balance is endangered, the Divine incarnates to restore truth, righteousness, and spiritual harmony.

verses.text_sanskrit:
परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम् |
धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय संभवामि युगे युगे || ८ ||
verses.transliteration:
paritrāṇāya sādhūnāṃ vināśāya ca duṣkṛtām |
dharmasaṃsthāpanārthāya saṃbhavāmi yuge yuge || 8 ||
verses.translation: To deliver the pious and protect the righteous, to annihilate the wicked miscreants, and to firmly re-establish the eternal principles of Dharma, I appear age after age (Yuge Yuge).
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna declares the triple purpose of His divine incarnation: protecting the virtuous seekers, neutralizing destructive evil forces, and re-anchoring society in sacred moral law (Dharma-samsthapana).

verses.text_sanskrit:
जन्म कर्म च मे दिव्यमेवं यो वेत्ति तत्त्वतः |
त्यक्त्वा देहं पुनर्जन्म नैति मामेति सोऽर्जुन || ९ ||
verses.transliteration:
janma karma ca me divyamevaṃ yo vetti tattvataḥ |
tyaktvā dehaṃ punarjanma naiti māmeti so'rjuna || 9 ||
verses.translation: One who truly understands the transcendental nature of My divine birth and activities, O Arjuna, upon leaving the mortal body, is never born again in this world of suffering, but attains My eternal abode.
verses.meaning: Contemplating the divine reality of Krishna's transcendental deeds (Lilas) dissolves all material karmic bonds. True spiritual realization of the Divine's nature liberates the soul from the wheel of birth and death (Samsara).

verses.text_sanskrit:
वीतरागभयक्रोधामन्मया मामुपाश्रिताः |
बहवो ज्ञानतपसा पूता मद्भावमागताः || १० ||
verses.transliteration:
vītarāgabhayakrodhā manmayā māmupāśritāḥ |
bahavo jñānatapasā pūtā madbhāvamāgatāḥ || 10 ||
verses.translation: Free from attachment, fear, and anger, fully absorbed in Me and taking refuge in Me alone, many in the past have been purified by the fire of wisdom (Jnana-tapas) and have attained My divine nature.
verses.meaning: Liberation is an accessible, well-trodden spiritual highway. By purifying the consciousness from the poisons of craving, fear, and hostility, and absorbing the mind in God through the austerity of spiritual knowledge, countless seekers have attained union with the Supreme.

verses.text_sanskrit:
ये यथा मां प्रपद्यन्ते तांस्तथैव भजाम्यहम् |
मम वर्त्मानुवर्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थ सर्वशः || ११ ||
verses.transliteration:
ye yathā māṃ prapadyante tāṃstathaiva bhajāmyaham |
mama vartmānuvartante manuṣyāḥ pārtha sarvaśaḥ || 11 ||
verses.translation: In whatever way living beings surrender unto Me and approach Me, in that very manner I reciprocate with them. O Partha, all humanity pursues My path in every way.
verses.meaning: A magnificent declaration of universal divine love and reciprocity. The Divine meets every seeker on their own terms—as Master, Friend, Child, Beloved, or the formless Absolute. Every genuine spiritual aspiration ultimately leads toward the One Supreme.

verses.text_sanskrit:
काङ्क्षन्तः कर्मणां सिद्धिं यजन्त इह देवताः |
क्षिप्रं हि मानुषे लोके सिद्धिर्भवति कर्मजा || १२ ||
verses.transliteration:
kāṅkṣantaḥ karmaṇāṃ siddhiṃ yajanta iha devatāḥ |
kṣipraṃ hi mānuṣe loke siddhirbhavati karmajā || 12 ||
verses.translation: Those who desire immediate success in fruitive actions worship the celestial deities in this world; for in the human world, success born of action is indeed attained very quickly.
verses.meaning: Most people chase short-term material results through transactional rituals. While worldly gains are swift, they are temporary and perishable. Only selfless devotion to the Supreme grants lasting inner peace and eternal liberation.

verses.text_sanskrit:
चातुर्वर्ण्यं मया सृष्टं गुणकर्मविभागशः |
तस्य कर्तारमपि मां विद्ध्यकर्तारमव्ययम् || १३ ||
verses.transliteration:
cāturvarṇyaṃ mayā sṛṣṭaṃ guṇakarmavibhāgaśaḥ |
tasya kartāramapi māṃ viddhyakartāramavyayam || 13 ||
verses.translation: The fourfold divisions of human society were created by Me according to aptitudes, qualities (Gunas), and work (Karma). Although I am the Creator of this system, know Me to be the non-doer and unchangeable.
verses.meaning: Social inclinations and vocations are divinely designed based on innate qualities (Gunas) and natural actions (Karma), rather than accidental physical birth. The Divine authors this natural order while remaining eternally detached and beyond all modes.

verses.text_sanskrit:
न मां कर्माणि लिम्पन्ति न मे कर्मफले स्पृह |
इति मां योऽभिजानाति कर्मभिर्न स बध्यते || १४ ||
verses.transliteration:
na māṃ karmāṇi limpanti na me karmaphale spṛhā |
iti māṃ yo'bhijānāti karmabhirna sa badhyate || 14 ||
verses.translation: Actions do not taint Me, nor do I possess any craving for the fruits of action. One who understands Me thus in truth does not become bound by the reactions of work.
verses.meaning: Because the Supreme Lord acts with zero selfish desire, He remains forever untouched by karmic consequences. A seeker who emulates this divine attitude of desireless action likewise breaks free from karmic imprisonment.

verses.text_sanskrit:
एवं ज्ञात्वा कृतं कर्म पूर्वैरपि मुमुक्षुभिः |
कुरु कर्मैव तस्मात्त्वं पूर्वैः पूर्वतरं कृतम् || १५ ||
verses.transliteration:
evaṃ jñātvā kṛtaṃ karma pūrvairapi mumukṣubhiḥ |
kuru karmaiva tasmāttvaṃ pūrvaiḥ pūrvataraṃ kṛtam || 15 ||
verses.translation: Knowing this truth, ancient seekers of liberation performed their duties. Therefore, you too should perform action, following in the footsteps of the ancients who acted in times of old.
verses.meaning: Great sages of yore attained spiritual freedom not by fleeing work, but by performing their duties with purified understanding. Sri Krishna urges Arjuna to walk this proven, luminous royal pathway of selfless action.

verses.text_sanskrit:
किं कर्म किमकर्मेति कवयोऽप्यत्र मोहिताः |
तत्ते कर्म प्रवक्ष्यामि यज्ज्ञात्वा मोक्ष्यसेऽशुभात् || १६ ||
verses.transliteration:
kiṃ karma kimakarmeti kavayo'pyatra mohitāḥ |
tatte karma pravakṣyāmi yajjñātvā mokṣyase'śubhāt || 16 ||
verses.translation: What is action and what is inaction? Even the wise and learned are bewildered on this point. I shall therefore explain unto you the true nature of action, knowing which you shall be freed from all evil.
verses.meaning: The distinction between true action and true inaction is subtle and often misunderstood. Merely moving the body is not necessarily action, and sitting idle is not necessarily inaction. Krishna prepares to reveal the esoteric truth of work.

verses.text_sanskrit:
कर्मणो ह्यपि बोद्धव्यं बोद्धव्यं च विकर्मणः |
अकर्मणश्च बोद्धव्यं गहना कर्मणो गतिः || १७ ||
verses.transliteration:
karmaṇo hyapi boddhavyaṃ boddhavyaṃ ca vikarmaṇaḥ |
akarmaṇaśca boddhavyaṃ gahanā karmaṇo gatiḥ || 17 ||
verses.translation: One must understand the nature of prescribed action (Karma), the nature of forbidden or prohibited action (Vikarma), and the nature of inaction (Akarma). Truly, profound and inscrutable is the path of action.
verses.meaning: The mechanics of karma are immensely intricate (Gahana karmano gatih). A spiritual seeker must discern righteous duty (Karma), harmful egoic deeds (Vikarma), and transcendental desireless action (Akarma) that produces no bondage.

verses.text_sanskrit:
कर्मण्यकर्म यः पश्येदकर्मणि च कर्म यः |
स बुद्धिमान्मनुष्येषु स युक्तः कृत्स्नकर्मकृत् || १८ ||
verses.transliteration:
karmaṇyakarma yaḥ paśyedakarmaṇi ca karma yaḥ |
sa buddhimānmanuṣyeṣu sa yuktaḥ kṛtsnakarmakṛt || 18 ||
verses.translation: One who sees inaction in action, and action in inaction—that person is truly wise among humanity; that person is a true yogi and the accomplished performer of all works.
verses.meaning: A pinnacle paradox of Vedic philosophy: The enlightened sage acts vigorously on the outside while remaining internally silent and untouched (inaction in action). Conversely, an idle person harboring inner cravings is actively generating karma (action in inaction).

verses.text_sanskrit:
यस्य सर्वे समारम्भाः कामसङ्कल्पवर्जिताः |
ज्ञानाग्निदग्धकर्माणं तमाहुः पण्डितं बुधाः || १९ ||
verses.transliteration:
yasya sarve samārambhāḥ kāmasaṅkalpavarjitāḥ |
jñānāgnidagdhakarmāṇaṃ tamāhuḥ paṇḍitaṃ budhāḥ || 19 ||
verses.translation: One whose undertakings are entirely free from selfish desires and personal egoistic plans, and whose actions have been burned away by the fire of wisdom—such a person is called a true sage (Pandita) by the wise.
verses.meaning: When the motivating fuel of selfish calculation (Kama-sankalpa) is eliminated, action ceases to generate karmic residue. The fire of spiritual knowledge incinerates all binding reactions, leaving the mind in perpetual purity.

verses.text_sanskrit:
त्यक्त्वा कर्मफलासङ्गं नित्यतृप्तो निराश्रयः |
कर्मण्यभिप्रवृत्तोऽपि नैव किञ्चित्करोति सः || २० ||
verses.transliteration:
tyaktvā karmaphalāsaṅgaṃ nityatṛpto nirāśrayaḥ |
karmaṇyabhipravṛtto'pi naiva kiñcitkaroti saḥ || 20 ||
verses.translation: Having abandoned all attachment to the fruits of action, ever-content, and independent of external circumstances, such a person does not perform any binding action, even while fully engaged in work.
verses.meaning: The self-realized soul is 'Nitya-tripta' (ever-satisfied in the Divine) and 'Nirashraya' (free from dependency on worldly props). Even while leading complex projects or battles, such a soul remains internally still and untainted.

verses.text_sanskrit:
निराशीर्यतचित्तात्मा त्यक्तसर्वपरिग्रहः |
शारीरं केवलं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् || २१ ||
verses.transliteration:
nirāśīryatacittātmā tyaktasarvaparigrahaḥ |
śārīraṃ kevalaṃ karma kurvannāpnoti kilbiṣam || 21 ||
verses.translation: Free from expectations, with mind and senses fully disciplined, having relinquished all possessiveness, performing work merely for the maintenance of the body—such a person incurs no sin.
verses.meaning: Living with minimal possessions and zero greed, acting solely for righteous bodily sustenance and service, the Karma Yogi remains as immaculate and unblemished as a drop of water on a lotus leaf.

verses.text_sanskrit:
यदृच्छालाभसन्तुष्टो द्वन्द्वातीतॊ विमत्सरः |
समः सिद्धावसिद्धौ च कृत्वापि न निबध्यते || २२ ||
verses.transliteration:
yadṛcchālābhasantuṣṭo dvandvātīto vimatsaraḥ |
samaḥ siddhāvasiddhau ca kṛtvāpi na nibadhyate || 22 ||
verses.translation: Content with whatever comes naturally without effort, rising above the dualities of life, free from envy, and equanimous in both success and failure—such a person is never bound, even while acting.
verses.meaning: Equanimity across all pairs of opposites (pleasure and pain, victory and defeat, profit and loss) ensures total psychological freedom. Free from jealousy (Vimatsara), the yogi's work becomes pure liberation.

verses.text_sanskrit:
गतसङ्गस्य मुक्तस्य ज्ञानावस्थितचेतसः |
यज्ञायाचरतः कर्म समग्रं प्रविलीयते || २३ ||
verses.transliteration:
gatasaṅgasya muktasya jñānāvasthitacetasaḥ |
yajñāyācarataḥ karma samagraṃ pravilīyate || 23 ||
verses.translation: For one who is devoid of attachment, liberated from ego, whose mind is firmly established in divine knowledge, and who performs work solely as a sacrifice (Yajna)—all karmic reactions dissolve entirely.
verses.meaning: When action is offered as a sacred sacrifice to the cosmos, the entire mass of past and present karma dissolves completely (Samagram praviliyate) into the ocean of transcendental consciousness.

verses.text_sanskrit:
ब्रह्मार्पणं ब्रह्म हविर्ब्रह्माग्नौ ब्रह्मणा हुतम् |
ब्रह्मैव तेन गन्तव्यं ब्रह्मकर्मसमाधिना || २४ ||
verses.transliteration:
brahmārpaṇaṃ brahma havirbrahmāgnau brahmaṇā hutam |
brahmaiva tena gantavyaṃ brahmakarmasamādhinā || 24 ||
verses.translation: The offering is Brahman; the oblation is Brahman; it is offered by Brahman into the sacred fire of Brahman. Brahman alone shall be reached by one who perceives Brahman in all actions.
verses.meaning: One of the most sacred and chanted verses of Sanatana Dharma. It reveals non-dual spiritual vision (Advaita Darshana): the instrument of offering, the food offered, the fire, the sacrificer, and the goal are all manifestations of the One Supreme Brahman.

verses.text_sanskrit:
दैवमेवापरे यज्ञं योगिनः पर्युपासते |
ब्रह्माग्नावपरे यज्ञं यज्ञेनैवोपजुह्वति || २५ ||
verses.transliteration:
daivamevāpare yajñaṃ yoginaḥ paryupāsate |
brahmāgnāvapare yajñaṃ yajñenaivopajuhvati || 25 ||
verses.translation: Some yogis perform sacrifice to the celestial deities, while other contemplative sages offer the sacrifice of the individual self into the transcendental fire of the Supreme Brahman.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna begins categorizing different dimensions of sacrifice (Yajna): from external ritual offerings to higher spiritual self-offering where the ego is surrendered into the infinite light of Brahman.

verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रोत्रादीनीन्द्रियाण्यन्ये संयमाग्निषु जुह्वति |
शब्दादीन्विषयानन्य इन्द्रियाग्निषु जुह्वति || २६ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrotrādīnīndriyāṇyanye saṃyamāgniṣu juhvati |
śabdādīnviṣayānanya indriyāgniṣu juhvati || 26 ||
verses.translation: Some offer the hearing and other senses into the fires of restraint; others offer sense objects such as sound into the fires of the senses.
verses.meaning: Ascetics practice sense-restraint by withdrawing their attention inward, while disciplined householders perceive sense objects with pure, sacred detachment, treating perception itself as a holy offering.

verses.text_sanskrit:
सर्वाणीन्द्रियकर्माणि प्राणकर्माणि चापरे |
आत्मसंयमयोगाग्नौ जुह्वति ज्ञानदीपिते || २७ ||
verses.transliteration:
sarvāṇīndriyakarmāṇi prāṇakarmāṇi cāpare |
ātmasaṃyamayogāgnau juhvati jñānadīpite || 27 ||
verses.translation: Others offer all the functions of the senses and the vital breath (Prana) into the fire of self-discipline (Atma-samyama-yoga), illuminated by spiritual knowledge.
verses.meaning: In deep meditation (Dhyana Yoga), the practitioner calms all sensory activity and regulates the subtle vital life-forces (Prana), offering them into the burning flame of Self-realization.

verses.text_sanskrit:
द्रव्ययज्ञास्तपोयज्ञा योगयज्ञास्तथापरे |
स्वाध्यायज्ञानयज्ञाश्च यतयः संशितव्रताः || २८ ||
verses.transliteration:
dravyayajñāstapoyajñā yogayajñāstathāpare |
svādhyāyajñānayajñāśca yatayaḥ saṃśitavratāḥ || 28 ||
verses.translation: Some offer their wealth in charity (Dravya-yajna); some offer severe austerities (Tapo-yajna); others practice the eightfold path of meditation (Yoga-yajna); while ascetics of strict vows offer scriptural study and knowledge (Svadhyaya-jnana-yajna).
verses.meaning: Yajna takes diverse forms suited to various human temperaments: philanthropic service, bodily self-mastery, mental meditation, and intellectual study of sacred truths. Every path sanctifies when performed selflessly.

verses.text_sanskrit:
अपाने जुह्वति प्राणं प्राणेऽपानं तथापरे |
प्राणापानगती रुद्ध्वा प्राणायामपरायणाः || २९ ||
verses.transliteration:
apāne juhvati prāṇaṃ prāṇe'pānaṃ tathāpare |
prāṇāpānagatī ruddhvā prāṇāyāmaparāyaṇāḥ || 29 ||
verses.translation: Others, dedicated to breath control (Pranayama), offer the outgoing breath into the incoming breath, and the incoming into the outgoing, arresting the movement of both.
verses.meaning: The science of Pranayama is celebrated here as a sacred internal offering. By mastering the incoming (Prana) and outgoing (Apana) vital currents, the yogi attains profound stillness of mind and heightened spiritual awakening.

verses.text_sanskrit:
अपरे नियताहाराः प्राणान्प्राणेषु जुह्वति |
सर्वेऽप्येते यज्ञविदो यज्ञक्षपितकल्मषाः || ३० ||
verses.transliteration:
apare niyatāhārāḥ prāṇānprāṇeṣu juhvati |
sarve'pyete yajñavido yajñakṣapitakalmaṣāḥ || 30 ||
verses.translation: Others, regulating their diet, offer the vital forces into the vital life-breaths. All these practitioners are knowers of sacrifice, and through sacrifice their sins are completely destroyed.
verses.meaning: Mindful dietary discipline harmonizes the body's internal energies. All authentic seekers who perform their respective disciplines with sacred intent cleanse their hearts and erase past karmic impurities.

verses.text_sanskrit:
यज्ञशिष्टामृतभुजो यान्ति ब्रह्म सनातनम् |
नायं लोकोऽस्त्ययज्ञस्य कुतोऽन्यः कुरुसत्तम || ३१ ||
verses.transliteration:
yajñaśiṣṭāmṛtabhujo yānti brahma sanātanam |
nāyaṃ loko'styayajñasya kuto'nyaḥ kurusattama || 31 ||
verses.translation: Those who partake of the nectar of the remnants of sacrifice attain the eternal Brahman. O best of the Kurus, this world is not for one who performs no sacrifice; how then can the next world be?
verses.meaning: One who lives a life of selfless offering tastes the immortal nectar of spiritual peace (Amrita) and attains the eternal Divine. Without selflessness and sacrifice, one can find neither happiness in this life nor fulfillment in the hereafter.

verses.text_sanskrit:
एवं बहुविधा यज्ञा वितता ब्रह्मणो मुखे |
कर्मजान्विद्धि तान्सर्वानेवं ज्ञात्वा विमोक्ष्यसे || ३२ ||
verses.transliteration:
evaṃ bahuvidhā yajñā vitatā brahmaṇo mukhe |
karmajānviddhi tānsarvānevaṃ jñātvā vimokṣyase || 32 ||
verses.translation: Thus, many varieties of sacrifices are spread out in the wisdom of the Vedas. Know that all of them are born of action. By understanding this truth, you shall be liberated.
verses.meaning: All forms of spiritual discipline require active, conscious engagement of body, mind, and intellect. Recognizing that work performed with spiritual understanding leads to liberation frees one from the fear of action.

verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रेयान्द्रव्यमयाद्यज्ञाज्ज्ञानयज्ञः परन्तप |
सर्वं कर्माखिलं पार्थ ज्ञाने परिसमाप्यते || ३३ ||
verses.transliteration:
śreyāndravyamayādyajñājjñānayajñaḥ parantapa |
sarvaṃ karmākhilaṃ pārtha jñāne parisamāpyate || 33 ||
verses.translation: The sacrifice of spiritual knowledge (Jnana-yajna) is far superior to any material sacrifice of physical objects, O scorcher of foes! For all action in its entirety, O Partha, culminates in spiritual wisdom.
verses.meaning: While material charity and ritual offerings are noble, the offering of one's ignorance into the light of divine knowledge is the highest sacrifice. All righteous action finds its ultimate fulfillment when it awakens transcendent wisdom.

verses.text_sanskrit:
तद्विद्धि प्रणिपातेन परिप्रश्नेन सेवया |
उपदेक्ष्यन्ति ते ज्ञानं ज्ञानिनस्तत्त्वदर्शिनः || ३४ ||
verses.transliteration:
tadviddhi praṇipātena paripraśnena sevayā |
upadekṣyanti te jñānaṃ jñāninastattvadarśinaḥ || 34 ||
verses.translation: Learn this truth by humble reverence (Pranipata), by sincere inquiry (Pariprashna), and by selfless service (Seva). The wise seers who have realized the ultimate truth will impart this knowledge unto you.
verses.meaning: A timeless classic on the authentic student-teacher relationship. Divine truth is transmitted through three essential attitudes: deep humility (Pranipata), honest and penetrating inquiry (Pariprashna), and devoted loving service (Seva) to an enlightened Master (Tattva-darshi).

verses.text_sanskrit:
यज्ज्ञात्वा न पुनर्मोहमेवं यास्यसि पाण्डव |
येन भूतान्यशेषेण द्रक्ष्यस्यात्मन्यथो मयि || ३५ ||
verses.transliteration:
yajjñātvā na punarmohamevaṃ yāsyasi pāṇḍava |
yena bhūtānyaśeṣeṇa drakṣyasyātmanyatho mayi || 35 ||
verses.translation: Having received this knowledge, O Pandava, you shall never again fall into such delusion; for by this wisdom you will see all living beings within your own Self, and then in Me.
verses.meaning: The ultimate vision of enlightenment: The seeker perceives the unity of all existence. Seeing all creatures first in one's own Self (Atman) and then in the Supreme Lord (Krishna) eradicates all sorrow, hatred, and illusion forever.

verses.text_sanskrit:
अपि चेदसि पापेभ्यः सर्वेभ्यः पापकृत्तमः |
सर्वं ज्ञानप्लवेनैव वृजिनं संतरिष्यसि || ३६ ||
verses.transliteration:
api cedasi pāpebhyaḥ sarvebhyaḥ pāpakṛttamaḥ |
sarvaṃ jñānaplavenaiva vṛjinaṃ saṃtariṣyasi || 36 ||
verses.translation: Even if you were the most sinful of all sinners, you shall cross over the vast ocean of all iniquities by the raft of spiritual knowledge alone.
verses.meaning: A sublime message of hope and divine mercy: No soul is permanently damned. The boat of Self-knowledge (Jnana-plava) possesses the power to carry even the most fallen individual safely across the turbulent sea of past sins.

verses.text_sanskrit:
यथैधांसि समिद्धोऽग्निर्भस्मसात्कुरुतेऽर्जुन |
ज्ञानाग्निः सर्वकर्माणि भस्मसात्कुरुते तथा || ३७ ||
verses.transliteration:
yathaidhāṃsi samiddho'gnirbhasmasātkurute'rjuna |
jñānāgniḥ sarvakarmāṇi bhasmasātkurute tathā || 37 ||
verses.translation: Just as a blazing fire reduces firewood to ashes, O Arjuna, even so does the fire of divine knowledge (Jnanagni) reduce all karmas to ashes.
verses.meaning: A magnificent metaphor: Centuries of accumulated karmic debt (Sanchita Karma) are burned to ashes in an instant when the blazing fire of Self-realization (Jnanagni) is kindled within the consciousness.

verses.text_sanskrit:
न हि ज्ञानेन सदृशं पवित्रमिह विद्यते |
तत्स्वयं योगसंसिद्धः कालेनात्मनि विन्दति || ३८ ||
verses.transliteration:
na hi jñānena sadṛśaṃ pavitramiha vidyate |
tatsvayaṃ yogasaṃsiddhaḥ kālenātmani vindati || 38 ||
verses.translation: In this world, there is nothing as sublime and purifying as spiritual knowledge. One who has attained perfection through Karma Yoga naturally realizes this wisdom within the Self in due course of time.
verses.meaning: Spiritual wisdom is the supreme purifier of human consciousness. When a seeker faithfully perseveres in the path of selfless duty (Yoga-samsiddha), this divine knowledge blossoms spontaneously within the heart at the ripe time.

verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रद्धावाँल्लभते ज्ञानं तत्परः संयतेन्द्रियः |
ज्ञानं लब्ध्वा परां शान्तिमचिरेणाधिगच्छति || ३९ ||
verses.transliteration:
śraddhāvāḻlabhate jñānaṃ tatparaḥ saṃyatendriyaḥ |
jñānaṃ labdhvā parāṃ śāntimacireṇādhigacchati || 39 ||
verses.translation: A person endowed with deep faith (Shraddha), deeply devoted to the truth, and having mastered the senses, attains supreme knowledge. Having attained this knowledge, one swiftly reaches transcendental peace (Param Shantim).
verses.meaning: The triple qualification for enlightenment: unshakable faith (Shraddha), single-pointed dedication (Tat-para), and mastery over the senses (Samyatendriya). Upon gaining this insight, the soul immediately enters the peace that surpasses all understanding.

verses.text_sanskrit:
अज्ञश्चाश्रद्दधानश्च संशयात्मा विनश्यति |
नायं लोकोऽस्ति न परो न सुखं संशयात्मनः || ४० ||
verses.transliteration:
ajñaścāśraddadhānaśca saṃśayātmā vinaśyati |
nāyaṃ loko'sti na paro na sukhaṃ saṃśayātmanaḥ || 40 ||
verses.translation: The ignorant, the faithless, and the perpetual skeptic go to ruin. For the doubting soul (Samshayatma), there is neither happiness in this world, nor in the next, nor anywhere.
verses.meaning: Cynicism and chronic doubt destroy human well-being. A mind paralyzed by suspicion can neither commit to noble worldly achievements nor experience spiritual joy. Faith and clear discernment are indispensable for inner peace.

verses.text_sanskrit:
योगसंन्यस्तकर्माणं ज्ञानसञ्छिन्नसंशयम् |
आत्मवन्तं न कर्माणि निबध्नन्ति धनञ्जय || ४१ ||
verses.transliteration:
yogasaṃnyastakarmāṇaṃ jñānasañchinnasaṃśayam |
ātmavantaṃ na karmāṇi nibadhnanti dhanañjaya || 41 ||
verses.translation: One who has renounced the fruits of action through Yoga, whose doubts have been severed by spiritual knowledge, and who is firmly established in the Self, O Dhananjaya (Arjuna), is never bound by actions.
verses.meaning: When all work is consecrated to the Divine (Yoga-sannyasta-karmanam), all doubts sliced away by wisdom's sword (Jnana-sanchinna-samshayam), and consciousness anchored in the True Self (Atmavantam), action becomes the expression of absolute freedom.

verses.text_sanskrit:
तस्मादज्ञानसंभूतं हृत्स्थं ज्ञानासिनात्मनः |
छित्त्वैनं संशयं योगमातिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ भारत || ४२ ||
verses.transliteration:
tasmādajñānasaṃbhūtaṃ hṛtsthaṃ jñānāsinātmanaḥ |
chittvainaṃ saṃśayaṃ yogamātiṣṭhottiṣṭha bhārata || 42 ||
verses.translation: Therefore, severing with the sword of wisdom (Jnanasina) this doubt residing in your heart, born of ignorance, establish yourself in Karma Yoga and arise for battle, O descendant of Bharata!
verses.meaning: The thunderous climax of Chapter 4: Sri Krishna commands Arjuna to wield the sword of divine wisdom, cut down the inner demons of hesitation and doubt, anchor his mind in Karma Yoga, and rise boldly to fulfill his sacred destiny.
